paragraphs: The X4 xDrive20d and xDrive30d have been part of the BMW X4 range since 2014, spanning two generations under one badge. The first-generation F26 (2014–2018) used the N47 4-cylinder diesel in the xDrive20d and the N57 6-cylinder diesel in the xDrive30d — though the N57 variant isn't confirmed for this specific application. From 2018, the second-generation G02 switched to the B47 (xDrive20d) and B57 (xDrive30d), which are generally reliable in this application. The X4 remains in production with these engines as of 2026.
about.boldParagraph: The X4 xDrive20d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre 4-cylinder diesel fitted to the first-generation X4 from 2014 to 2015. Known for timing chain stretch — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N47 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre 4-cylinder diesel fitted to the current-generation X4 from 2018 onwards. Generally reliable in this application — no confirmed issues for this specific variant. We replace timing chain, injector seals and gaskets as standard on every B47 rebuild.

A 3.0-litre 6-cylinder diesel fitted to the current-generation X4 from 2018 onwards. Generally reliable in this application — no confirmed issues for this specific variant. We replace timing chain, injector seals and gaskets as standard on every B57 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because BMW X4 xDrive20d can use the N47 or B47 or B57 engine code, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N47, B47 or B57) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic X4 quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
